text:
maria: Heads-up — after merge #3125 we're seeing a perf regression on small-batch (1-4) TTI. CI runtimes spiked ~2.5x on last canary and users hit higher p95. Reproduced locally on g4dn: compile storm + large kernel compile picked repeatedly.
ryan: ugh. which change in #3125 looks suspicious? autotune heuristic tweak?
maria: autotune heuristic for kernel selection renamed pick_policy -> pick_policy_v2; new scoring now prefers single-kernel that reduces memory churn but increases compile time for short sequences. logs: 
```
[2026-02-12T14:03:12Z] compile: selected kernel "fused-attn-v3" for model transformer-xl seq=32 batch=2
[2026-02-12T14:03:12Z] compile: start compile /tmp/compile-xyz
[2026-02-12T14:03:13Z] kvcache: bucket invalidated for session 0x7fae
[2026-02-12T14:03:13Z] serve: miss->cold for prefix 0x12a4, resetting state
[2026-02-12T14:03:14Z] compile: finished in 1.1s
[2026-02-12T14:03:14Z] request: p50 120ms -> 320ms
```
maria: notice the kvcache invalidation right after compile start — looks like the compile path is touching cached pointers and triggering eviction under the new kernel path.
sanjay: can you paste the autotune scoring diff?
maria: diff snippet: 
```diff
- score = mem_weight*mem_cost + latency_weight*latency_cost
+ score = mem_weight_v2*mem_cost_v2 + latency_weight*latency_cost + compile_penalty*compile_cost
```
maria: compile_penalty was meant to avoid large compiles, but bug in cost estimator returns 0 for short sequences so it favors kernels that need JIT and blowup.
alice: CI flagged this as a perf failure on the canary rollout, infra blocked the release. ops-bot posted the rollout-blocker alert: see https://deployments/reports/3125
dev-bot: deploy-check: canary failure detected for release/3125 — blocking rollout (rule: p95_latency_increase > 1.5x) :rotating_light:
ryan: immediate mitigation options? force old heuristic, disable v2, or pin kernel map to previous compiled artifacts.
sanjay: easiest is to flip feature flag AUTOTUNE_V2=false on canary and start bisect. we can also add quick guard: if sequence_length < 64 and batch_size <=4, prefer legacy kernel.
maria: I pushed a quick config override to canary: AUTOTUNE_V2=false. rerunning perf tests.
ops-bot: config updated in canary environment by maria at 2026-02-12T14:12:05Z
ryan: good. also create a replay job to reproduce without live traffic. can you add flamegraphs?
maria: uploaded flamegraph: https://artifacts/internal/flame/3125-canary.svg — shows heavy time in compile_hotpath and kvcache mutex spin.
sanjay: looks like compile path takes a global cache lock when picking new kernel, which races with prefix cache writes and triggers a full invalidation. we should avoid global lock or make compile async.
alice: test matrix: small-batch seq 16/32 batch 1-4, with/without kvcache priming, old vs new autotune. I'd like the bisect owner?
ryan: I'll bisect across commits in #3125. tagging @maria and @sanjay for pointers.
maria: noted. running bisect now, will post minimal repro and PR to revert the autotune change if we can't get a quick fix.
ryan: if bisect points to the scoring change, revert + patch to fix cost estimator. if it's the compile-side locking, we may need a short revert plus follow-up async compile patch.
maria: update — with AUTOTUNE_V2=false canary p95 back to baseline. rolling back rollout hold.
ops-bot: rollout-blocker cleared for release/3125 by maria
alice: please file a postmortem stub and add the test case to perf-ci to catch this.
sanjay: I'll open a PR for a fix that: 1) corrects compile_penalty estimator for short sequences 2) decouples kernel selection from kvcache lock.
maria: thanks. adding checklist to the ticket: add regression unit in perf-ci, ensure canary feature flags for autotune, and add prometheus metric for compile_rate and kvcache_evictions. :memo:
ryan: thumbs-up. keep updates in this thread.
